messages:
alex_support: FYI — Customer reported a big tail latency regression after turning on tool/function calling + structured output validation on their route. p95 jumped from ~450ms -> ~1.2s, p99 spiked to ~2.3s. They say it started after enabling schema validation.

alex_support: Repro steps they gave: curl to /v1/generate with tool router enabled and schema in `functions` payload. They included a trace id: trace:rn-0a1b2c3d. Sending logs below.

alex_support: sample request header they used:
```
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate \
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer <key>' \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{"route":"/customer/chat","model":"gptx-8b","tool_router":true,"functions":[{"name":"search","parameters":{"type":"object","properties":{"q":{"type":"string"},"filters":{"type":"object"}}}}],"input":"Find docs about batching"}'
```

alex_support: from their sampled logs (timestamps in ms since req start):
```
parse_req: 4ms
auth: 3ms
router_match: 12ms
schema_validation: 1250ms
model_inference: 820ms
post_process: 18ms
-> total: ~2.1s (peak p99)
```

alex_support: They also noted that if they disable the `functions` param entirely latency returns to baseline.

mia_engineer: thanks alex. tagging @sam_runtime and @jenna_oncall. this smells like sync schema validation or remote validator call blocking the pipeline. do we have the validator host in the trace? can ops share span breakdown?

sam_runtime: looking. trace rn-0a1b2c3d shows an extra RPC to router-validator: validator.redwood.svc cluster on the critical path. spans: router.resolve (10ms), validator.compile (1,180ms), validator.respond (5ms). seems the validator does AJV compile+validate per-request, not using compiled cache for these schemas.

sam_runtime: the `functions` schemas in this customer's payload are large (deep refs + examples). AJV compile can be expensive first time. but 1.1s suggests we're compiling repeatedly. i suspect we missed compile-cache due to ephemeral schema ids.

jenna_oncall: can we hotfix by making validation async (fire-and-forget) or moving to streaming validation so it doesn't block model tokens? customer is in production and impacted.

mia_engineer: yes. quick mitigations: 1) roll back the route flag for that customer to disable structured validation 2) enable precompile/cache in validator service (fast) 3) short term: use small schemas or truncate examples in payloads.

sam_runtime: config snippet to make validator async/opt-in (temporary):
```json
{
  "route": "/customer/chat",
  "tool_router": true,
  "structured_validation": {
    "mode": "async",
    "timeout_ms": 50
  }
}
```

sam_runtime: note: async mode will accept output and validate in background; if it fails we send regression alert but we won't block the response path. good stopgap.

alex_support: customer asked if schema validation runs server-side only or in the model runtime. they believe it was blocking token streaming (they saw no streaming chunks until validation finished).

sam_runtime: confirm — current implementation performs validation before streaming response to ensure conformance. that's why p99 jumped. streaming while validating requires incremental validators or moving validation to post-processing.

mia_engineer: longer term fixes: precompile schemas on upload (persist schema fingerprint -> compiled AJV fn), add a small LRU cache keyed by schema fingerprint, and instrument metrics on compile duration. also allow per-route validation policy (sync/async/off).

mia_engineer: also we should add a router optimization: if functions list matches a cached fingerprint, skip RPC to validator and run local compiled fn. avoids network hop.

devrouter_bot: created ticket INFRA-9876 to add schema precompile cache + metrics. linked to this thread.

jenna_oncall: immediate action for customer: roll their route back to pre-validation config and confirm latency returns to baseline. alex, can you patch their tenant flag?

alex_support: will do now and will ask them to run same repro. pinging once done.

alex_support: patched tenant flag -> validation disabled for that route. customer re-tested and reported p95 ~470ms, p99 ~620ms. much improved.

alex_support: shared repro curl and new trace id rn-0a1b2c3d-2. logs show no validator span anymore.

sam_runtime: good. next steps: 1) deploy AJV compile-cache patch (high priority) 2) add metric histogram for validator compile time to catch future regressions 3) add an opt-in async validation policy and document tradeoffs. I'll take the deploy (sam_runtime).

mia_engineer: assign owners and timelines here: sam -> patch+deploy by EOD tomorrow, devops -> add metric + alert by EOD today (jenna), alex -> confirm rollback + customer comms (today).

jenna_oncall: putting follow-up in incidents channel and scheduling a 30m triage in 30m to confirm no other customers affected.

ops_bot: incident created: INC-2026-041, severity: S2, subscribers: infra, runtime, support.

alex_support: customer happy with rollback for now but wants a durable fix. i'll keep them updated and collect any other examples of large schemas.

sam_runtime: also note: function/tool router adds small per-request overhead even without validation (route lookup, mapping). for high QPS flows we should benchmark router hot path and consider inlining small routers in the runtime. adding a perf test to project board.

mia_engineer: thanks everyone. summary: rollback done (customer unblocked), patch for compile-cache + metrics in flight, follow-up triage scheduled. I'll update this thread after deploy.

alex_support: thanks — closing loop with customer now. will post any further anomalies here. :thumbsup:
